scope_note: Third-pass modeled contribution review retains two low-confidence, last-resort sensitivities after direct-source exhaustion. The first converts the contractor-reported 1.4 MW whole-facility redundant available-power nameplate into annual electricity throughput at 25%, 50% and 100% utilization, with the high endpoint explicitly treated as a mathematical ceiling. It does not apply PUE because the source does not distinguish utility-input, critical IT or redundant-path capacity. The second combines the trade-reported approximately 70 electricians, the 234-day groundbreaking-to-report interval and BLS's near-period Detroit-area mean electrician wage into a 25%, 50% and 100% worker-duration wage-payroll sensitivity. It is limited to the reported electrician subset and excludes benefits, overtime, other trades and residence effects. No operating staffing, investment, supplier, community, fiscal/public-cost, emissions, water or county-effect model passes: no source requires continuous on-site coverage; the MCE $4.8 million field is undefined and postdates a site redesign; separate real and personal accounts lack bills and payments; the recovered City subsidy report omits this project; and no site-linked operating, recipient or counterfactual inputs exist.

sources.title: Detroit-Warren-Dearborn, MI — May 2016 OES Metropolitan and Nonmetropolitan Area Occupational Employment and Wage Estimates
sources.notes: The official area table reports 10,210 electricians (SOC 47-2111), a $32.05 median hourly wage, a $29.16 mean hourly wage and a $60,650 annual mean wage for May 2016. The model uses the mean hourly wage as a near-period area benchmark, not as a project wage, union scale, prevailing wage or certified-payroll observation.

estimates.label: Whole-facility annual electricity-throughput sensitivity

period.label: Annualized engineering sensitivity from the completed-facility 1.4 MW available-power nameplate

scope.label: Whole Quicken Loans Technology Center at 1401 Rosa Parks Boulevard; no tenant or server-room allocation

interval.interpretation: The reported 1.4 MW available-power nameplate is annualized at 25%, 50% and 100% utilization. The high endpoint is the mathematical continuous-load ceiling for that nameplate, not a forecast, true-value bound or confidence interval.

parameters.name: reported_available_power

provenance.detail: Electrical-contractor description of completed-facility redundant available power

parameters.transformation: Converted to kW and multiplied by annual hours and utilization

estimates.confidence_rationale: The 1.4 MW figure is project specific, but the source does not define its meter boundary, distinguish utility-input from IT load, or report utilization. Metered electricity, occupancy, peak demand and site PUE remain unavailable.
estimates.decision_relevance: Provides an explicit order-of-magnitude annual throughput range and theoretical ceiling without relabeling capacity as measured consumption or extending it to cost or emissions.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Utility meter data, bills, peak demand, capacity boundary, occupied IT load, site PUE, tenant allocation, electricity price, renewable share and emissions

assumptions: The reported 1.4 MW is used once; redundant paths or generators are not added.
Utilization scenarios are 25%, 50% and 100% solely for sensitivity.
No PUE multiplier is applied because the capacity boundary is undefined.
The result remains whole-facility and is not allocated by lease share, floor area or server-room count.

limitations: No meter reading, utility bill or observed load factor.
The source's available-power terminology may not equal utility-input or critical IT capacity.
The interval is a scenario range, not a statistical or physical bound below the stated ceiling.
No electricity cost, emissions, output or fiscal effect is inferred.
estimates.notes: Resource-use sensitivity only. The direct 1.4 MW capacity claim remains the authoritative observation; this model is not an economic contribution and must not be added to monetary records.

estimates.label: Electrician-only construction wage-payroll sensitivity

period.label: Documented groundbreaking-to-trade-report interval; individual worker duration is parameterized

scope.label: Approximately 70 IBEW Local 58 electricians reported on the Quicken Loans Technology Center project

interval.interpretation: Seventy electricians are valued at the BLS $29.16 Detroit-area mean hourly wage, 40 hours per week and 25%, 50% or 100% of the 234-day elapsed construction interval. This is a worker-duration sensitivity, not observed payroll, a true-value bound or a confidence interval.

parameters.name: reported_electricians

provenance.detail: Approximately 70 electricians reported employed on the project since groundbreaking

parameters.transformation: Multiplied by weekly hours, elapsed weeks, area mean wage and duration share

parameters.name: elapsed_construction_interval

provenance.detail: 234 calendar days from May 20, 2014 groundbreaking through January 9, 2015 trade report

parameters.transformation: Sets the maximum modeled elapsed duration

parameters.name: area_mean_electrician_wage

provenance.detail: May 2016 Detroit-Warren-Dearborn mean hourly wage for SOC 47-2111 electricians

parameters.transformation: Applied as a near-period wage benchmark

provenance.detail: Straight-time full-week benchmark; overtime is excluded
Each reported electrician averages one quarter of the elapsed interval
Each reported electrician averages one half of the elapsed interval
All reported electricians work the full elapsed interval

estimates.confidence_rationale: Worker count and project dates are source anchored, but the count is approximate, actual worker start/stop dates and hours are absent, and the BLS area mean is from May 2016 rather than project payroll.
estimates.decision_relevance: Bounds the only construction trade with a project-specific worker count while keeping wage payroll separate from total labor income, total construction employment, supplier spend and household effects.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Certified payroll, individual hours and duration, 2014-2015 union wage classifications, overtime, benefits, other trades, worker residence and total construction labor

assumptions: The approximate 70-person count is used without scaling to other trades.
Each worker averages 25%, 50% or 100% of the 234-day elapsed interval.
A 40-hour straight-time week is used; overtime is excluded.
The May 2016 BLS area mean is a near-period wage benchmark, not a claimed Local 58 or project wage.

limitations: BLS wage timing and occupation mix may differ from project classifications.
No benefits, overtime, payroll taxes, proprietor income or other trades are included.
No worker-residence or local-household capture is inferred.
The high endpoint assumes full-interval duration for every reported electrician and is not an empirical upper bound.
estimates.notes: Electrician wage-payroll sensitivity only. Do not present as total construction labor income, total payroll, job-years, local payroll or an additive component of the undefined $4.8 million contractor-page value.
